chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated — from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, who said: Ya'qub ibn Yaqtin narrated to me —
He said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) about a man who emits madhī while he is in salat, whether from desire or without desire.

His statement 'madhī [requires] wudu' is interpreted as expressing astonishment rather than as an informative declaration — as if, given the well-known and manifest [ruling] that wudu is not required because of it, he said: 'This is something that requires wudu?!' As for kissing and touching the genitalia, these two do not nullify wudu. And that which indicates this...

key_terms.التَّعَجُّبُ: ta'ajjub — rhetorical astonishment; al-Tusi's interpretive device explaining that the Imam's statement was an exclamation of surprise, not a legal declaration
key_terms.الْإِخْبَارُ: ikhbār — an informative, declarative statement; contrasted here with ta'ajjub as the two possible readings of the Imam's ambiguous words
key_terms.الْمَذْيُ: madhī — pre-seminal or prostatic fluid emitted during sexual excitement, whose jurisprudential ruling regarding ritual purity is the central subject of this hadith
key_terms.يَنْقُضَانِ: yanquḍān — 'they (two) nullify/break'; the key jurisprudential verb establishing that kissing and touching the genitalia do not invalidate wudu

ai.seo_question: Does madhī (pre-seminal fluid) emitted during salat require wudu according to Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Ya'qub ibn Yaqtin asked Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) whether madhī (pre-seminal fluid) emitted during salat requires wudu, whether triggered by desire or not. Shaykh al-Tusi interprets the Imam's response — which on its surface says madhī requires wudu — as rhetorical astonishment at the question, not a legal ruling, since the well-established position is that madhī does NOT require wudu. Al-Tusi further states that kissing and touching the genitalia likewise do not nullify wudu, and proceeds to cite proofs for this ruling.
word_analysis: then indeed the two of them
